title: Indian-American Former Google Executive Sheetal Wrzesien Shot Dead in Georgia; Husband Arrested on Murder Charges
excerpt: The 57-year-old Georgia Tech alumna and tech leader was killed in a domestic violence incident at her Cobb County home. Her 23-year-old son survived after being shot and fleeing to neighbours for help.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Sheetal Wrzesien, a former Google executive, was shot dead by her husband in Georgia.
  • Her 23-year-old son survived the shooting and sought help from neighbors.
  • Kirk Wrzesien faces five felony charges, including felony murder.
  • Sheetal was a respected tech leader and advocate for women in STEM.
  • The community is in shock over the domestic violence incident.
Tragic Domestic Violence Incident
›Sheetal Wrzesien, 57, shot dead at home.
›Son Jason, 23, survived after fleeing.
›Kirk Wrzesien, 56, arrested without resistance.
›Charges: 1 felony murder, 2 aggravated assault.
›Incident occurred on July 11, 2023.
Sheetal Wrzesien, a 57-year-old Indian-American technology executive and former Google engineering leader, was shot dead by her husband at their home in Cobb County, Georgia, in what police have described as a domestic violence incident. The couple's 23-year-old son, Jason, was also shot but survived after fleeing the house to seek help from neighbours. Kirk B. Wrzesien, 56, was arrested at the family's residence on Laurel Creek Trail in Smyrna, near Atlanta, and is being held without bond at the Cobb County Adult Detention Center, [The Hindu Business Line reported](https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/). ## What Happened According to the Cobb County Police Department, officers responded to reports of gunfire at the Wrzesien home shortly before 8 p.m. on the evening of July 11. They found Jason Wrzesien outside the house with gunshot injuries and rushed him to a nearby hospital, where he underwent emergency surgery. Inside the residence, officers discovered Sheetal Wrzesien with multiple gunshot wounds. She was pronounced dead at the scene, [Fox 5 Atlanta reported](https://worldmalayaleevoice.com/indian-origin-ex-google-techie-sheetal-wrzesien-shot-dead-in-us-husband-arrested). Investigators said the shooting stemmed from an escalating domestic confrontation. Kirk Wrzesien was apprehended at the scene without resistance and now faces five felony charges: one count of felony murder, two counts of aggravated assault with a deadly weapon, and two counts of possession of a firearm during the commission of a felony. ## A Career in Technology Sheetal Wrzesien was a respected figure in Atlanta's technology community. She graduated with a Computer Science degree from the Georgia Institute of Technology in 1994 and went on to build a career spanning more than two decades in tech leadership. At Google, she served as Engineering and Operations Lead for the company's Data Governance, Content Management, and Customer Relationship Management systems, [according to her LinkedIn profile](https://worldmalayaleevoice.com/indian-origin-ex-google-techie-sheetal-wrzesien-shot-dead-in-us-husband-arrested). She later returned to Google as a Marketing Technology Advisor in the Android division. At the time of her death, Sheetal had been working as Senior Director at GoTo Foods. She had also led large-scale mobile and e-commerce digital transformation projects for major American retailers, including The Home Depot.

Beyond her corporate work, Sheetal served on the academic advisory board of Georgia Tech's College of Computing and was widely recognised for mentoring young professionals and encouraging women to pursue STEM careers. ## Community in Shock Neighbours expressed disbelief at the violence in what they described as a quiet, family-oriented neighbourhood. "I've seen him doing yard work. Really nice guy. Very social neighbour," neighbour Peter Lee told Atlanta News First. "It's a terrible tragedy."
Community Reaction
›Neighbors describe the area as quiet and family-oriented.
›Peter Lee: 'Really nice guy. Very social neighbor.'
›Community in disbelief over the tragedy.
›Investigation focused solely on domestic incident.
Sheetal had spent her early years across England, India, and Ghana before settling in the United States, where she became a pillar of Atlanta's Indian-American and tech communities. Authorities have confirmed the investigation remains focused on the domestic incident. No additional suspects are being sought. Jason Wrzesien's current medical condition has not been publicly updated.
